For the best five, a short, specific pitch that offers something useful to that audience and is not a generic press release. Contact details are checked, and no pitch is sent without the owner's approval.

title: Interview 10 prospects to find the objections that stop them signing up
description: The team guesses why prospects do not sign up. Success means ten short conversations with people who run or lead a cohort programme, from bootcamps, schools or training teams, using the same five questions. The output is a one-page summary of the top objections ranked by how often they came up, with a direct quote for each (used with permission), and three recommended changes to the website or pricing page. Participants are real, not invented, and any who decline are replaced rather than made up.

title: Get the Zedu mobile app's Google Play and App Store listings ready to convert by Fri 20 Nov
description: Many people in Africa find apps in the store first, and a weak listing loses them before they install. Write the store listings for the Zedu mobile app. Work under this goal: keyword research for the store search (education, team chat, class, community, with sources); app name and subtitle options within each store's limits; short and full descriptions; text and order for 6-8 screenshots, matched to the real app; a "what's new" note; and a review of 5 competing listings (Slack, Discord, Teams, Google Classroom, Telegram) for what works. Every feature listed is checked in the live mobile app. This is separate from the web directories goal. Done when: complete listing copy and screenshot plans for both stores are delivered and approved.

title: Answer 30 real questions about running study groups and cohorts on Quora, Reddit and forums by Fri 20 Nov
description: People ask every day how to run a study group, manage a class on WhatsApp, or keep a bootcamp cohort engaged. Helpful answers bring steady, trusted traffic for years. Find 30 real, recent questions on Quora, Reddit (for example r/edtech, r/Teachers, r/learnprogramming, r/Nigeria), Nairaland and Stack Exchange. Draft a genuinely helpful answer to each that stands on its own, and mention Zedu only where it truly fits, disclosed as "I work on Zedu". Follow each community's self-promotion rules. Agents find the questions and draft; a person posts from their own account. Done when: 30 answers are drafted and reviewed, and a tracker lists each question, its link and whether the answer is posted.

title: Plan and write a month of LinkedIn and X posts for bootcamp operators and course leads
description: Zedu has no regular voice where its audience spends time. Success means a four-week content calendar with 12 original posts for LinkedIn and X, each tied to a real problem cohort operators have, with a hook, the body, a call to action and the Zedu page it points to. Posts are useful on their own, do not attack named products, contain no invented statistics or testimonials and are written to be approved by a person before posting.

title: Create an education keyword map and a publishing plan for the next quarter
description: Nobody has mapped which searches Zedu should be found for. Success means a keyword map of at least 60 education-community searches grouped by intent (learn, compare, buy), each with a reason it fits, the page that should target it, and whether that page exists. The map ends with a ranked publishing plan for the quarter that names the 10 pages to write or improve first and why. Search volumes and difficulty are taken from named tools or marked as estimates, and no figure is invented.

title: Write 20 short video scripts showing one Zedu tip each by Fri 13 Nov
description: Short vertical videos (TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts) are where students and young professionals in Africa discover tools. Write 20 scripts of 20-40 seconds, each showing one useful thing in Zedu (for example: set up a class in a minute, mute a busy channel, find an old file, use threads so announcements don't get lost). Each script has a hook in the first 2 seconds, the on-screen steps matched to the live app, captions, a caption for the post and hashtags. These are many short tips, not one long product demo. A team member records them. Done when: 20 scripts are written, checked against the live app and reviewed.

title: Build a help centre with answers to the 20 questions new organisers ask most
description: New organisers get stuck on the same first-week questions: creating an organisation, inviting members, setting roles, starting a call, sharing files. Success means a help centre of 20 short answers, each tested step by step against the live product, with the exact menu names and one screenshot or short description of the result. Questions are chosen from real support messages, tickets and Ziki issues, not guessed. Each answer is under 250 words and links to the next related answer.

title: Translate the homepage, pricing and sign-up pages into French for francophone Africa by Fri 27 Nov
description: Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Cameroon, Benin, Rwanda and others run large bootcamps and universities in French, and Zedu is English-only. Translate and adapt (not just translate word for word) the homepage, the pricing page and the sign-up page into French for West and Central African readers. Work under this goal: a glossary of product terms (channels, Buzz, workspace) with the French to use; the three pages in French with titles and meta descriptions; and a review of each page by a fluent French speaker before it is approved. Keep the same claims as the English pages; nothing new is promised. Done when: three pages and the glossary are delivered and approved by a fluent reviewer.

title: Interview early Zedu users and publish short, honest case studies
description: Marketing has no proof from real users. Success means three to five short interviews with people who have actually used Zedu in a cohort, school or training programme, each turned into a one-page case study that states the problem, what they used Zedu for and what changed. Every quote and number is checked with the person and used only with their written permission. No case study is invented, composed or exaggerated. If fewer than three real users agree, the goal is met with the ones who did and the gap is reported.

title: Write clear product pages for the four core features: channels and DMs, Buzz calls, file management and threads
description: Visitors can only choose Zedu if each core feature has a page that explains it in plain language. Success means one page per feature for channels and DMs, Buzz calls, file management and threads. Each page says what the feature does, who it helps and a typical day-to-day example, in under 600 words, with a title under 60 characters, a description under 160 and a clear next step. Facts come from the live product, and anything the product does not do yet is left out.

title: Start a public "What's new in Zedu" page with monthly release notes by Fri 13 Nov
description: Users and prospects can't see how fast Zedu improves, and the team has no place to announce changes. Set up a "What's new" page and write the first release notes. Work under this goal: a release notes template (headline, what changed, who it helps, a screenshot note and a link to the help article); a back catalogue covering the changes shipped from August to October 2026, taken from the public zedu-fe, zedu-be and app repos and checked in the live app; and a short monthly routine for the team to keep it going. Only shipped changes are listed, in plain English with no internal ticket jargon. Done when: the template, the page copy and three months of release notes are written and reviewed.

title: Get Zedu featured in Nigerian tech press
description: Local tech press is read by the founders and schools Zedu wants. Done when: a pitch about Zedu as a Nigerian-built learning platform is sent to TechCabal, Techpoint Africa, Benjamindada and Techeconomy with a one-page fact sheet (every number confirmed with the team first), each pitch tracked in Amp's press funnel, and at least one piece of coverage or a clear answer from each outlet.

title: Rewrite the homepage message so a visitor understands what Zedu is within five seconds
description: A first-time visitor should be able to say what Zedu is, who it is for and what to do next without scrolling. Success means a rewritten headline, subheadline and primary call to action for the homepage, with two alternative versions and a short reason for each choice, plus a list of the duplicated blocks on the page to remove or shorten. Every claim comes from Zedu's own pages or product, and no claim is stronger than what the product does. The rewrite uses the words the audience uses (cohort, bootcamp, course lead) instead of generic software language.

title: Publish a step-by-step guide to running a cohort on Zedu
description: Show the product working for its main use case: a bootcamp sets up a workspace, one channel per cohort, Buzz for live classes, files and threads for assignments. Done when: a 1,200-word guide with real screenshots of the live app, every step checked on zedu.chat, ready to publish on Zedu's blog and share with leads.

title: Find learning communities that run on WhatsApp and Telegram today
description: Developer groups, study groups and professional associations that organise on WhatsApp or Telegram feel the pain Zedu solves: lost threads, scattered files, no live sessions in one place. Done when: 25 active communities with their size, platform, what they teach and a one-line pitch angle for each, from public information only.

title: Find 30 universities and polytechnics running online or hybrid programmes
description: Give the Universities solution page real targets. Done when: 30 Nigerian and wider African institutions with distance or hybrid programmes, the department or unit that would buy a learning platform, and a public source for each, ranked by fit.

title: Publish a gallery of 8 ready-made Zedu workspace templates by Fri 20 Nov
description: A blank workspace is the hardest part of starting. Templates show people how to set Zedu up for their situation in minutes. Write 8 templates: a 12-week bootcamp cohort, a university course, a secondary school class, a study group, a hackathon, a community of practice, a small startup team, and an internship programme. Each template lists the channels to create and what each is for, the roles and who gets them, pinned messages and first posts to copy, and a weekly routine, all using features that exist in the live app today. Each also gets a short page intro, title and meta description so the gallery can rank for "how to organise a ... online". Done when: 8 templates are written, checked against the live app and reviewed.

title: Build a lead list of 50 Nigerian bootcamps and tech academies that run cohorts
description: Cohort programmes are Zedu's core market: a channel per cohort, Buzz for live classes, files and threads for assignments. Done when: 50 qualified bootcamps, tech hubs and academies running cohort programmes, each with city, rough size, programmes, a public contact page and the tool they use today if visible, with a source link for every fact. No personal contact details that aren't publicly listed for business enquiries.

title: List Zedu in education and EdTech directories
description: General SaaS directories are already covered by another goal. This one is the education side: EdTech product indexes, school-software marketplaces and African EdTech lists where schools and bootcamps look for tools. Done when: at least 15 suitable directories are found with their requirements and cost, and Zedu is submitted to the free ones, each tracked in Amp with its status and listing link.

title: Map the search terms schools and bootcamps use to find a learning platform
description: Find the words programme managers, instructors and bootcamp founders in Nigeria and across Africa type when looking for a tool like Zedu (for example "online class platform for bootcamps", "Slack alternative for schools", "virtual classroom with attendance"). Done when: 40 keywords with search intent, rough volume and the Zedu page each one should land on, with the source of every volume figure.

title: Make unknown zedu.chat addresses return a real 404
description: A made-up address like zedu.chat/this-page-does-not-exist answers HTTP 200 with the home page (a soft 404, checked 22 Oct 2026). That wastes Google's crawl and hides broken links. Done when: unknown addresses return status 404 with a helpful not-found page, the affected URLs are listed, and Search Console shows no soft-404 warnings for zedu.chat.

title: Write the welcome email sequence and a monthly newsletter for new signups
description: People who sign up for Zedu hear nothing useful from it afterwards. Success means a welcome sequence of short emails that take a new organiser from signup to their first channel, first invite and first call, plus a monthly newsletter template with a repeatable structure. Every email has one purpose, one call to action, a subject line under 50 characters and plain, honest wording with no invented statistics or customer quotes. Each email says what the reader does next inside Zedu and names the page or setting where they do it. Drafts are ready to paste into an email tool and are checked against the real product screens.

title: Make zedu.chat's marketing pages meet WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility by Fri 20 Nov
description: Schools and universities often have to buy tools that are accessible, and accessible pages are also easier for search engines to read. Audit every public marketing page on zedu.chat against WCAG 2.2 AA: colour contrast, alt text, heading order, keyboard navigation, visible focus, form labels, link text and motion. Work under this goal: an audit table per page (issue, WCAG rule, where it is, how to fix it, and the file in zeduchat/zedu-fe); a short accessibility statement the site can publish; and a re-check after fixes using axe or Lighthouse plus a keyboard-only walk-through. Done when: every public marketing page has no AA failures in the re-check and the accessibility statement is approved.

title: Add structured data (JSON-LD) to Zedu's marketing pages
description: The home page and the Schools page have no JSON-LD on production (checked 22 Oct 2026), so Zedu can't get rich results. Done when: every marketing page (home, products, solutions, pricing, about, download) has the schema it needs (Organization, SoftwareApplication, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList), the JSON-LD is ready to paste or merged, and each page passes Google's Rich Results Test.

title: Give zedu.chat's home page a real title and a share preview
description: Today the live home page's <title> is just "Home" and it has no og:image, so Google results and WhatsApp, LinkedIn and X previews look empty (checked 22 Oct 2026). Done when: the home page has a title under 60 characters and a meta description under 155 that say what Zedu is for, a 1200x630 share image, matching Open Graph and Twitter tags, and before/after preview screenshots from a link-preview checker.

title: Get every public zedu.chat page indexed on Google and Bing by Fri 6 Nov
description: A page that isn't indexed can't rank, however good its title or speed. Check which public zedu.chat pages Google and Bing have actually indexed (site: searches, URL Inspection, Bing Webmaster Tools), and find why the missing ones are left out: no sitemap entry, a noindex tag, a wrong canonical, blocked in robots.txt, or no internal links pointing to them. Work under this goal: an index coverage table (URL, indexed on Google, indexed on Bing, reason if not); a corrected sitemap.xml and robots.txt; and a step-by-step for a team member to verify the site in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools and submit the sitemap. This is about indexing only, not titles, descriptions or speed. Done when: every public marketing page shows as indexed on both Google and Bing, with the coverage table updated.

title: Build a beginner-friendly library of resources for running a cohort programme
description: Bootcamp operators and course leads who are new to running cohorts search for practical help: how to onboard a cohort, how to keep learners active, how to run office hours and weekly check-ins. Zedu has no resources for them. Success means a small library of original, practical guides, each built around a real question a new cohort operator asks, written in plain language, with a clear next step that points to the relevant Zedu page. Each guide has a title under 60 characters, a description under 160, one main search question it answers, and sources for any figure it uses. No guide makes a claim about Zedu that is not on Zedu's own pages.

title: Publish comparison and alternative pages for the cohort software buyers search for
description:
Zedu has no comparison content at all, and comparison pages are how software buyers who already know the category choose a vendor. The searches are already there: "Discord alternatives for bootcamps", "Discord vs LMS", "Slack alternative for cohort programs", "best platform for running a bootcamp". The live results for those terms are almost entirely consumer and IT tools, with nothing written for the education use case, which means the page is available to be written rather than fought for.

Each page covers one comparison: what each product is structurally good at, who it is right for, who it is wrong for, and where the honest overlap is. Zedu's own claims are taken from Zedu's pages, and no named competitor is characterised beyond what it publicly states. Pages are scoped one comparison each, with a title under 60 characters, a description under 160, a FAQ that matches real queries, and the internal links to add.

title: Grow Zedu's pipeline and turn its traffic into signups
description:
Zedu's marketing site has been worked on for being found. It has not been worked on for being chosen. Six goals in this project cover search visibility, page speed, metadata and content, and none of them owns the two things that decide whether a visitor becomes a customer: who the platform should be reaching, and what stops them signing up.

This goal covers both.

On the pipeline side: the audience is training and education operators — bootcamp operators, corporate training teams running cohort programmes, university and K-12 course leads — and nobody has identified them yet. The task types for lead hunting and press outreach exist and are worth fifty points each, and not one task of that kind has been created in this project.

On the conversion side, the measurement is in the site's own pages. The line "Launching a bootcamp? Let's build a pricing model that fits your cohort size" appears on both the homepage and the pricing page. The same "Got a Question? We Have an Answer" block is repeated on the homepage, the pricing page and all three product pages. The homepage embeds the full pricing table that /pricing exists to hold, and the same segment cards appear on the homepage and on each of the three solution pages. So the questions a visitor asks before they sign up are answered in several places at once and in different words, and the strongest versions of them are diluted.

Success means a qualified list of prospects with a named reason each one fits, at least one pitch sent to a real outlet that genuinely covers the audience, and a set of conversion recommendations for the duplicated blocks above, with the duplicates consolidated and the surviving version saying the thing more directly.

title: Research competitors and the market
description: Understand who Zedu competes with and how they market themselves. Focus on comparing competitors’ features, pricing, messaging, SEO keywords and channels, then turning the findings into opportunities Zedu can act on.

title: Find partnership and outreach leads
description: Build lists of organisations that could use or promote Zedu, such as tech bootcamps, universities, communities and newsletters. Focus on accurate contact details, short outreach messages, and tracking who has been contacted.

title: Build backlinks through directory submissions
description: Get Zedu listed on relevant startup, product and tech directories (e.g. Product Hunt, BetaList, TechCabal) and earn quality backlinks. Focus on finding the right directories, preparing listing content, submitting, and tracking which ones go live.

title: Improve Zedu on-page content SEO
description: Optimise Zedu’s page titles, meta descriptions, headings, keywords, alt text and internal links so each page ranks better and drives more organic traffic.
